title: 26.2 A Wideband Replicas-Rejection Digital Transmitter Using Joint-Digital-Analog Interpolation and Filtering in 28nm CMOS
problem: Wideband digital transmitters (DTXs) struggle with sampling replicas at f_LO + n×f_s that fall close to signal band, violating emission masks and requiring high sampling rates + expensive off-chip RF filters. Supporting multiple sub-6 GHz standards (LB/HB) forces separate RF chains, increasing area and complexity.
motivation: Sub-6 GHz wireless spectrum crowding and multi-standard support (LTE/5G/WiFi) demand integrated, single-chain wideband DTXs with efficient replica suppression to reduce BOM cost and power.
method: Joint digital-analog interpolation and filtering strategy: optimized digital polyphase filter reduces per-channel sampling rate while maintaining high output rate; wideband quadrature DPA with IQ-cell-sharing and transformer-based load modulation; analog interpolation integrated into DPA circuit to suppress replicas. Unified architecture eliminates need for separate LB/HB chains.
key_novelty: Co-design of digital polyphase filtering + analog interpolation within DPA suppresses sampling replicas without high-speed off-chip filtering, enabling single unified wideband DTX.
contributions: Unified wideband DTX eliminates separate LB/HB RF chains, reducing area/complexity
Joint digital-analog interpolation/filtering suppresses replicas to meet emission masks without off-chip filters
Optimized polyphase architecture reduces per-channel sampling rate and DSP power
Transformer-based load modulation improves DPA linearity and efficiency

metrics.other: Wideband coverage, replica suppression, area/power reduction vs. separate chains

limitations: Abstract lacks specific metrics (ACPR, EVM, power consumption, chip area).
primary_theme: Joint digital-analog DTX for wideband sub-6 GHz
